Zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression

Source: R/zinbreg.R
zinbreg.Rd

Fits the ZINB model of Lambert (1992) with an NB2 count component: $$P(Y_i = 0) = \pi_i + (1-\pi_i) f_{NB}(0;\mu_i,\theta), \quad P(Y_i = y) = (1-\pi_i) f_{NB}(y;\mu_i,\theta),\ y \ge 1,$$ with \(\log\mu_i = x_i^\top\beta + o_i\) (count model) and \(\mathrm{logit}\,\pi_i = z_i^\top\gamma\) (zero-inflation model). Estimation is by the EM algorithm: the E-step computes the posterior probability \(\tau_i\) that each zero is a structural zero, and the M-step fits a fractional-response logistic regression for \(\gamma\) and a weighted NB regression (weights \(1-\tau_i\)) for \((\beta,\theta)\), both by IRLS. No general-purpose optimizer is used. The parameterization is the same as pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin").

Usage

zinbreg(formula, data, offset, control = zinbreg_control())

Arguments

formula

A two-part formula y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2: count-model covariates before |, zero-model covariates after it. Without |, the same covariates are used in both parts (as in pscl::zeroinfl()). offset() terms are allowed in the count part only.

data

A data frame containing the variables in formula.

offset

Optional count-model offset (e.g. log(exposure)), evaluated in data.

control

A list from zinbreg_control().

Value

An object of class "zinbreg": a list with components

coefficients

List with count (\(\beta\)) and zero (\(\gamma\)).

vcov

Estimated covariance matrix of \((\hat\beta, \hat\gamma, \log\hat\theta)\): the inverse of the observed information, from the analytic Hessian of the observed-data log-likelihood. Row/column names are count_*, zero_*, and Log(theta), as in pscl::zeroinfl().

theta, SE.theta, SE.logtheta

\(\hat\theta\), its standard error (delta method), and the standard error of \(\log\hat\theta\).

score

Analytic score vector at the estimates (should be ~0).

loglik, loglik_path

Maximized observed-data log-likelihood, and its value at every EM iteration (non-decreasing).

df

Number of estimated parameters (\(p + q + 1\)).

fitted.values

\(E(Y_i) = (1-\hat\pi_i)\hat\mu_i\).

mu, pi

Count-model means \(\hat\mu_i\) and zero probabilities \(\hat\pi_i\).

iter, converged

Number of EM iterations and convergence flag.

boundary

TRUE if the zero-inflation component vanished (all \(\hat\pi_i < 10^{-8}\)); a warning is then issued.

y, offset, nobs

Response, count offset, number of observations.

call, terms, xlevels, contrasts, model

Information used by predict() and other methods.

Details

EM does not produce standard errors, so after convergence the observed information \(-H\) of the observed-data log-likelihood with respect to \((\beta, \gamma, \log\theta)\) is computed from analytic second derivatives and inverted.

References

Lambert, D. (1992). Zero-inflated Poisson regression, with an application to defects in manufacturing. Technometrics, 34(1), 1-14.

See also

zinbreg_control(), nbreg()

Examples

# Simulated ZINB data: one covariate in each part
set.seed(1)
n <- 500
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n), z = rnorm(n))
structural_zero <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-1 + d$z))
d$y <- ifelse(structural_zero == 1, 0,
              rnbinom(n, size = 1.5, mu = exp(1 + 0.5 * d$x)))
fit <- zinbreg(y ~ x | z, data = d)
fit$coefficients
#> $count
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>   0.9979526   0.4374179 
#> 
#> $zero
#> (Intercept)           z 
#>   -1.653210    1.253677 
#> 
fit$theta
#> [1] 1.157176
